historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr, judgmentally preferred over equity_5yr_cagr and the reported/owner-FCF CAGRs
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (0.83%) and owner-FCF CAGRs (50-81%) diverge enormously from revenue CAGRs (6-9%) and from each other. This is a cyclical-recovery artifact, not a real growth-rate signal: FY2020 was a COVID-driven trough (a $15.7B goodwill impairment crushed FY2020 equity and owner-FCF was only $120M that year on a 0.6% margin), so every CAGR anchored to 2020 or 2021 is inflated by the low base. EPS CAGRs are not computable cleanly because FY2020-2022 EPS was negative. Revenue CAGR is used as the primary anchor here instead of the house default (equity CAGR), because equity CAGR for a company that took a ~$16B one-off impairment mid-history is not a meaningful measure of underlying compounding -- the divergence is disclosed rather than silently resolved by picking equity CAGR by default.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 revenue lands near guidance as the Precision Sensors divestiture and a partial-year Chart contribution roughly net out against continued OFSE softness; from FY2027 record IET backlog conversion, a full year of Chart, and New Energy scaling drive mid-to-high single-digit growth tapering to a 2.75% terminal rate, with EBITDA margin expanding gradually from ~17.9% to ~19.8% as the higher-margin IET/Chart mix grows.
scenario_narratives.bull: LNG turbomachinery dominance and AI data-center power demand compound faster than guided, Chart delivers full cost synergies plus commercial cross-sell upside, and OFSE stabilizes rather than deteriorates as global energy demand holds up -- growth reaches low-double-digits in the middle years with margin expanding to 22%.
scenario_narratives.bear: NOC capex discipline (led by Saudi Aramco) widens into a broader oil-price downcycle just as BKR carries ~$10B of fresh Chart-related debt; competitive share loss to Siemens Energy/Mitsubishi Heavy Industries in turbomachinery accelerates, Chart integration disappoints on synergies, and New Energy/data-center order growth normalizes lower -- revenue contracts in year 1 and growth stays low-single-digit throughout, with margin compressing on OFSE mix.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Baker Hughes is valued as a cyclical industrial operating company on a strict owner-FCF DCF: SBC (small for this name, 0.73-1.0% of revenue) fully expensed with the share count held flat, no interest-income adjustment since BKR carries net debt rather than net cash, and a 10-year explicit horizon because the owner-FCF margin is still recovering from the FY2020 COVID/impairment trough toward a mature IET-driven margin level. The single largest judgment in this build is the Chart Industries acquisition's balance-sheet impact: the June 2026 pre-close snapshot (debt $16.25B, cash $15.7B) is a transitory financing float, not a steady state, so net debt is instead estimated as FY2025's clean net debt ($2.37B) plus the observed net new acquisition debt raised ($10.17B), for a total of $12.5B -- a judgment estimate pending the first post-close (Q3 2026) balance sheet, which should be used to refresh this figure at the next update rather than re-deriving it from scratch.
key_risks_to_valuation: Post-close balance sheet (net debt, share count from the merger consideration mix) is estimated, not observed -- refresh from the Q3 2026 10-Q as soon as it is filed
OFSE oil-price cyclicality and Saudi Aramco/NOC capex discipline could push results toward the bear case
Chart Industries integration risk on a $13.6B, only-just-closed deal -- synergy delivery and cultural/operational integration are unproven
Stock has already re-rated ~40%+ YTD in 2026 on the AI/data-center power narrative; base case does not assume that narrative simply continues to expand the multiple further

SBC understated if BKR has an equity-award withholding-tax cash outflow not captured in the available XBRL facts (industrials typically have small such populations, but this was not independently verified against the actual 10-K text since Extracted/ is empty for this ticker)

inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 cash flow statement SBC add-back ($203M, 0.73% of revenue); no separate equity-award withholding-tax line found in available XBRL facts, so the cash-flow add-back is used as-is (industrials typically have small, mostly-cash-settled award populations vs. US tech, so this understatement is expected to be minor)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5% built on a USD risk-free rate (~4.2% 10yr UST, Sep-2026) + ~5.3pp ERP/beta premium for a cyclical industrial with elevated (post-Chart) leverage; toward the upper end of the house 8-11% range for US industrials given the fresh ~$10B of acquisition debt and OFSE's oil-price cyclicality, offset by IET's growing long-cycle backlog reducing overall cash-flow volatility
inputs.lease_treatment: No material finance/operating lease adjustment made -- BKR's lease footprint is not disclosed as a swing factor in the Analysis JSON and reported FCF/OCF show no unusual lease distortion; leases are treated as embedded in reported operating costs (no separate deduction, no lease liabilities added to net debt)
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- no minority interest disclosed as material in Analysis JSON or filings reviewed
inputs.notes: OWNER-FCF DCF (owner_fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md section 7f only, for cyclical risk-charged-once discipline; no currency/lease/NCI adaptations needed -- USD filer, USD quote, no material leases or NCI disclosed). Routed per SKILL.md: large-cap operating company (oilfield services + industrial energy technology), cyclical -- owner-FCF DCF is the correct model, not a bank/REIT/LIC variant. FRESH BUILD, no prior DCF/Drivers file existed. base_revenue is FY2025 actual ($27,733M), NOT the FY2026 guidance figure ($27.35B) -- guidance is booked as the modelled outcome of year-1 assumptions (Precision Sensors divestiture drag, partial-year Chart contribution, OFSE softness from NOC capex discipline, offset by IET backlog conversion), landing Year-1 modelled revenue close to the $27.35B guided figure by construction rather than by using it as the compounding base. NET DEBT: FY2025 clean net debt was $2,372M (total debt $6,087M - cash $3,715M, both from 10-K/XBRL). The Chart Industries acquisition (closed July 2026, ~$13.6B enterprise value, cash-and-stock) is captured via net_debt=12,538 = FY2025 net debt (2,372) + net new acquisition debt (10,166, the observed total-debt delta between FY2025 ($6,087M) and the Q2 2026 10-Q pre-close snapshot ($16,253M) taken 2026-06-30). The Q2 2026 balance sheet itself (debt $16,253M / cash $15,727M / net debt only $526M) is a TRANSITORY pre-close snapshot -- the $15.7B cash was raised-but-unspent acquisition financing sitting on the balance sheet for weeks before the July close, not a steady-state cash position, so it is not used directly as the anchor. This is a judgment estimate in the absence of a post-close (Q3 2026) balance sheet; total_debt/cash inputs above are therefore synthetic placeholders (total_debt=FY2025 actual, cash=negative plug) purely to make net_debt reconcile to 12,538 for the engine -- net_debt is the governing figure. SHARES: 992,674,071 basic shares outstanding per the Q2 2026 10-Q cover page (SEC XBRL dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, as of 2026-07-23); grossed up to ~1,005M for full dilution (~1.3% historical basic-to-diluted gap). Share count held FLAT per house rule -- SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count; buyback_cash of $384M (FY2025 financing-activity repurchases) funds that flat count. SBC is genuinely small for BKR (0.73-1.0% of revenue historically) -- an industrial company, not a heavy stock-comp issuer -- so house and street bases are close but not identical; band_position is reported normally (not null), since SBC is nonzero. TERMINAL CAP: capped at 11x (below the 20x house default and below the 12-15x 'cyclical' floor suggested for structurally slower/cyclical names) to reflect OFSE's history of trading at high-single-digit to low-teens EV/EBITDA through cycles, blended with IET's better long-cycle multiple; Gordon at 9.5% WACC / 2.75% terminal growth already sits below this cap in the base case (see valuation output), so the cap does not bind in base but is retained as a discipline against runaway bull-case multiple expansion. HORIZON: 10 years -- owner-FCF margin is still recovering from the FY2020 downcycle trough (0.6% in 2020 to 8.4% in FY2025) and is not yet at a mature steady state; a 5-year horizon would capitalize an immature, still-ramping margin. RISK CHARGED ONCE: cyclicality (oil price, NOC capex discipline, OFS margin volatility) and Chart integration risk are priced in the flows via the three scenarios and their probability weights, not via a stacked WACC premium or per-scenario WACC differences (same 9.5% WACC used in all three scenarios).

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted estimate (~1,005M) from the 992.67M basic count on the Q2 2026 10-Q cover page (2026-07-23), grossed up ~1.3% for options/RSUs consistent with BKR historical basic-diluted gap. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows -- charging both would double-count.

bear.narrative: OFSE demand deteriorates as Saudi Aramco and other NOCs extend capex discipline into a broader oil-price downcycle, compounded by a global economic slowdown that also pressures industrial capex; Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries continue winning LNG/turbomachinery contracts at BKR's expense, eroding the historical ~90% share and IET order growth well short of the Horizon 2 (>$45B) outlook; Chart Industries integration proves harder than expected -- promised $325M synergies slip and management distraction shows up in execution misses elsewhere, while the ~$10B of acquisition debt raises interest burden into a weaker demand environment; New Energy and data-center power orders slow as AI capex growth normalizes and policy support for hydrogen/CCUS softens. Margin compresses modestly from mix (lower-margin OFSE a larger relative share as IET growth stalls) rather than collapsing outright, consistent with IET's long-cycle backlog providing a floor even in a downcycle. Working capital capture is more negative (-12%) reflecting slower collections and inventory build typical of an OFS downcycle.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue lands close to guidance (~-1.4% vs FY2025 actual) as the ~$1.15B Precision Sensors divestiture and a partial-year, transition-heavy Chart contribution roughly offset continued OFSE softness from NOC/Aramco capex discipline. From FY2027 the first full year of Chart contribution, continued IET record-backlog conversion (Horizon 2 orders >$45B through 2028, data-center power systems demand), and New Energy scaling to $2.4-2.6B lift growth into the mid-single-to-high-single digits, tapering as the LNG/data-center order cycle matures and OFSE settles into a slower-growth, mature oilfield-services trajectory. EBITDA margin expands gradually from FY2025's ~17.9% (implied) toward ~19.8% as IET's higher-margin, more recurring aftermarket/services mix grows as a share of the business and Chart's cost synergies ($325M targeted by year 3) phase in. Cash tax rate ramps modestly above the FY2025 effective cash rate toward a normalized ~23% as one-off credits/NOLs are used up. Working capital is modelled with a small NEGATIVE capture (-8%) on revenue growth, consistent with BKR being a project/equipment manufacturer and distributor (inventory + receivables growth outpacing payables as revenue grows), the opposite sign from a prepaid-subscription business.

bull.narrative: LNG turbomachinery near-monopoly (~90% share) converts the full Horizon 2 IET order pipeline (>$45B through 2028) with minimal share loss to Siemens Energy/Mitsubishi; AI data-center power demand keeps compounding beyond the $1B/quarter run-rate already seen in Q1 2026, becoming a durable, largely oil-price-uncorrelated order stream; Chart integration delivers both the full $325M cost synergies ahead of schedule AND meaningful commercial synergies (cross-selling cryogenic/LNG equipment) management has flagged as unquantified upside; New Energy scales faster than the $2.4-2.6B FY2026 guide as CCUS/hydrogen policy support holds; OFSE stabilizes as oil demand growth persists through the 'energy demand decade' management describes, so NOC capex discipline does not worsen. Margin expands faster and further (to 22%) as the higher-margin IET/Chart mix scales and operating leverage on record backlog conversion flows through.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 11x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the house default 15% to 25% to reflect three concurrent, correlated risks specific to this build: (1) genuine oilfield-services cyclicality with a live downside catalyst already flagged by management (Saudi Aramco capex pressure), (2) integration risk on a large, only-just-closed $13.6B acquisition (Chart, the third-largest deal in company history) financed with ~$10B of fresh debt, raising financial risk if the cycle turns before deleveraging, and (3) a stock that has already re-rated ~40%+ YTD on the AI/data-center narrative, leaving less room for a soft landing on any of the above. Bull weight trimmed to 25% (from the 35% house default) because the bull case requires several correlated things to go right simultaneously -- full Chart synergy capture AND continued LNG share dominance AND sustained AI power-demand order growth AND no OFSE deterioration -- rather than a single independent catalyst.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
